items.title: Establish CDO governance, DesignOps and artifact decision rights
items.outcome: A large design organization can work in parallel because every artifact, decision, review, approval, SLA, file and escalation has one accountable owner and a durable record.
items.context: Without explicit decision rights, a large team multiplies contradictory sitemaps, components and approvals. The Chief Design Officer must govern outcomes without becoming an unbounded production queue.
scope: RACI for CDO, DesignOps, research, service design, platform design, systems, content, accessibility, UX engineering and Design QA
D0 through D9 gate definitions, evidence, approver, expiry and reopen conditions
Figma project, file, page, branch, library, version, review and archive topology
Design review SLAs, WIP limits, decision log, exception format and escalation
Artifact naming and ownership rules that prevent concurrent edits to shared pages
acceptance_criteria: Every design artifact class has exactly one accountable role and at least one independent verifier
CDO approval is limited to D2, D6, D8, shared-system major releases and material change exceptions
A stale approval, unresolved blocking comment or missing evidence prevents the dependent gate from closing
The Figma topology names files, pages, branch naming, publishing, archive and restoration behavior
A simulated two-squad conflict resolves through the decision log without either squad overwriting shared work
contracts_schema: Publishes machine-readable artifact statuses, gate identifiers, approval roles, version and expiry fields consumed by T-UXR-06
security_privacy: Research and design files never contain real financial records, raw messages, credentials or unredacted support evidence
Figma and research access use least privilege, offboarding and an auditable external-sharing policy
observability: Review age, blocked artifact count, approval expiry, WIP by squad and reopened-gate count without participant or financial content
tests: Expired approval and unresolved-blocking-comment failure fixtures
rollout_rollback: Adopt before any shared design file is created; migration imports existing research as read-only evidence
Rollback freezes publishing and retains the decision history rather than returning to unowned files
non_goals: Replacing product management or security approval
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. DesignOps owns governance and generated indexes; platform squads own separate Figma files and cannot edit governance-controlled regions.
definition_of_done: Governance record and machine-readable gate vocabulary merged
CDO and every named discipline lead approve their decision rights
Conflict, expiry and access-control tests pass
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Create the ethical research operations and participant evidence system
items.outcome: Research can recruit representative participants and produce trustworthy evidence without collecting unnecessary financial data or exposing household participants to one another.
items.context: Personas and flows are only as good as their evidence. Finance and coercive-control research introduces consent, retention, recruitment and disclosure risks that ordinary usability operations do not address.
scope: Research consent, screening, incentive, recording, note, anonymization, retention and deletion policy
Recruitment matrix across debt, income, permission attitude, literacy, language, disability, device and connectivity
Independent household and safe-exit recruitment that prevents paired disclosure
Versioned plans, scripts, raw-note access, synthesis, limitations and finding disposition
Synthetic financial scenario and device-reset protocol
acceptance_criteria: No study requires a participant to expose a real account, message, credential, balance or household disclosure
Every study records target sample, exclusions, method, limitation, retention and decision it can change before recruitment
Recruitment coverage is measurable against the matrix and convenience sampling is labeled rather than hidden
Household participants are never recruited or scheduled in a way that reveals one member's private response to another
Expired recordings and notes become unreadable and deletion evidence is retained without participant identity
contracts_schema: Research-plan, participant-code, evidence, limitation and finding-disposition schemas with no financial-value field
security_privacy: Research identity mapping is separated from notes, encrypted, access-limited and never copied to design files
Safe-exit and coercion studies use specialist review and a participant-controlled stop path
observability: Recruitment coverage, withdrawal, evidence age and undispositioned finding count without participant identity
tests: Planted financial-data and credential rejection tests
rollout_rollback: A policy failure pauses recruitment and preserves only the minimum audit record
non_goals: Using production telemetry as participant identity
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. UX Research owns plans and evidence; designers receive anonymized findings, while Legal and Security review policy without editing synthesis.
definition_of_done: Research operations pack and repository structure merged
Privacy, Legal, Accessibility and UX Research Lead approvals recorded
Synthetic-data, retention and safe-recruitment tests pass
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Validate personas, jobs, financial mental models and exclusion risks
items.outcome: The planning personas and jobs are supported, revised or rejected by launch-market evidence before navigation, language and critical journeys harden around team assumptions.
items.context: The product serves debt, privacy, household, split, AI and operator contexts with different mental models. A demographic persona deck would not tell teams how people interpret balances, payoff, sharing or uncertainty.
scope: Contextual interviews and artifact walkthroughs covering the twelve PRODUCT.md persona hypotheses
Jobs, triggers, desired progress, anxieties, workarounds, vocabulary and trust signals
Financial literacy, disability, language, constrained-device and permission-denial needs
Behavioral segments and anti-personas based on incompatible or unsafe needs
Evidence-backed persona/JTBD cards with confidence, contradictions and research gaps
acceptance_criteria: Every retained persona cites evidence, sample limitation and at least one observable design consequence
No persona is defined only by age, income or an invented quote
Debt, manual/privacy-first, automation, household/safe-exit, split, web power-user and operator jobs are explicitly covered
Terms participants misunderstand or use differently are fed into T-CNT-01
Contradictory evidence changes the persona model or creates a dated research gap; it is never averaged away
contracts_schema: Persona, job, evidence, confidence, risk and design-consequence records referenced by the coverage registry
security_privacy: Published personas contain no participant quote or combination that can re-identify a person
Unsafe or out-of-scope jobs such as lending recommendations are marked non-target rather than converted into features
observability: Persona evidence age, confidence, uncovered recruitment cells and unresolved contradiction count
rollout_rollback: Personas are versioned hypotheses and may split or retire as evidence changes
A major persona change reopens affected journeys, not every design artifact
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. UX Research owns evidence and persona records; service and platform designers consume versioned IDs and propose changes through findings.
definition_of_done: Persona and JTBD set merged with evidence and limitations
UX Research Lead, Product, Accessibility and CDO approvals recorded
All traceability and exclusion tests pass
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Map end-to-end journeys and service blueprints across every channel
items.outcome: Every critical user and operator outcome is represented as a cross-channel journey and service blueprint with frontstage, backstage, data, policy, failure and recovery ownership.
items.context: A screen list cannot expose handoff gaps between Android capture, API processing, web correction, operator fulfillment and user notification. Service blueprints make those seams reviewable before implementation.
scope: Current and target journeys for activation, debt planning, capture/clarification, import, goals, sharing, split, AI, billing, rights and support
Operator blueprints for rights, refunds, unmask/elevation, provider change and incidents
Frontstage screens, system handoffs, backstage services, contract events, policy gates and telemetry
Failure, offline, timeout, revocation, partial completion, escalation and rollback branches
Moments of truth and measurable outcome per journey
acceptance_criteria: Every critical registry flow belongs to a journey with a named success and failure recovery
Every cross-platform handoff identifies the authoritative service and what the receiving surface can safely show
Rights, sharing and billing blueprints include clock, audit, notification and reversal behavior
No backstage step requires raw message egress, client-side money arithmetic or unauthorized detail access
Journey gaps create owned backlog items before IA approval
contracts_schema: Journey and blueprint step IDs map to screen, flow, service, contract event, policy and telemetry identifiers
security_privacy: Blueprints mark data classification and authorization at every boundary
Household and operator journeys include abuse cases and safe failure, not only cooperative actors
observability: Journey completion, abandonment, correction, recovery and escalation signals with content-free event shapes
rollout_rollback: Target journeys supersede current maps with links; no historical evidence is overwritten
A service or contract change reopens only blueprints that reference it
non_goals: Declaring a happy path complete when recovery is absent
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Service Design owns blueprint topology; platform designers own frontstage detail and service teams verify backstage feasibility in review.
definition_of_done: Journey and blueprint set merged with stable identifiers
Product, Architecture, Security, Operations and IA approvals recorded
Coverage, handoff and abuse-case tests pass
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Approve platform allocation, sitemaps and navigation architecture
items.outcome: Android, customer web and admin have complete, tested and intentionally different information architectures so no implementation squad invents navigation or hides an orphaned feature.
items.context: The backlog names features but not where users find them. A shared feature set does not imply shared navigation: Android is capture-first, web is analysis-heavy and admin is queue/role driven.
scope: Platform allocation matrix with parity, divergence and handoff rationale
Android compact/expanded sitemap and primary navigation
Customer-web signed-out and signed-in responsive sitemap
Admin role-aware sitemap with absent-route rules
Card sorting, tree testing, labels, search/discovery and deep-link destinations
acceptance_criteria: Every screen registry entry has exactly one navigation parent or documented external/system entry
Every planned feature is reachable in a tree test without relying on global search
Android primary navigation stays within platform limits and defines expanded-width adaptation
Web narrow layouts remain complete and admin unauthorized destinations are absent rather than disabled
Cross-platform divergences record user/job rationale and CDO approval
contracts_schema: Platform allocation, route, navigation parent, deep-link and role-visibility records consumed by the coverage registry
security_privacy: Navigation labels and denied destinations never reveal hidden household, support or operator data
Admin route absence is tested as authorization behavior, not decoration
observability: Tree-test success, first-click correctness, navigation backtrack and orphan-route counts
tests: Card sort and tree test with representative personas
Compact, expanded and narrow-web navigation walkthrough
rollout_rollback: IA versions are immutable after D1; later changes carry migration and deep-link compatibility
Rollback restores the previous route map and redirect table
non_goals: Using one sitemap unchanged on all platforms
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. The IA Lead owns canonical route topology; platform squads own layout and interaction within their allocated routes.
definition_of_done: Platform allocation and three sitemaps merged
Tree-test evidence and unresolved findings dispositioned
IA, Security, Accessibility and CDO approvals recorded
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Publish the screen, flow, component and test traceability registry
items.outcome: Every persona, journey, flow, screen, state, component, diagram, design artifact, implementation ticket and QA owner is connected by a schema-validated registry.
items.context: A large plan can look comprehensive while still omitting a state or leaving a frontend ticket without design. The registry turns coverage into a failing contract rather than a spreadsheet review.
scope: Versioned JSON registry and JSON Schema for personas, journeys, user stories, flows, screens, components and diagrams
Stable IDs, cross-references, criticality, platform, surface type, state vocabularies and owner tickets; immutable artifact versions and approval expiry live in the D6 handoff and readiness schemas
Validator checks for uniqueness, dangling references, orphan screens, unused components and missing design/QA ownership
Exhaustive partition of every Android, web and admin repository ticket into mapped frontend work or a reasoned non-frontend exclusion
Frontend-ticket design prerequisite and release-gate coverage checks
Generated human-readable coverage summary
acceptance_criteria: Every Android, web and admin repository ticket is either mapped to at least one screen or flow or has an explicit non-frontend rationale
Every critical flow has a persona, journey, ordered screens, design owner, implementation owner and independent QA owner
Every referenced component and state exists and every component is used or explicitly foundational
The validator fails on a missing screen, dangling ID, unclassified client ticket, platform mismatch, unmapped implementation ticket, missing D6 dependency or release-gate bypass
Coverage output is deterministic and reviewable in pull requests
contracts_schema: experience-coverage.schema.json and stable ID vocabularies for P, J, F, S, C and D records
security_privacy: Registry metadata contains no user, participant, financial or credential content
Security-critical screens must name privacy and authorization states
observability: Coverage percentages by platform, criticality, state, design owner, implementation owner and QA owner
tests: Dangling-reference, duplicate-ID and orphan-screen negative tests
rollout_rollback: Land schema and initial complete registry together; partial coverage cannot be marked green
Rollback keeps the last valid registry and blocks new frontend readiness
non_goals: Storing screenshots or research evidence in JSON
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. DesignOps owns schema and generated summaries; platform squads edit only records assigned to their ID ranges and validator prevents collisions.
definition_of_done: Schema, registry and validator merged
All existing frontend tickets mapped
Deliberate negative tests pass
DesignOps, QA and Architecture approvals recorded
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Select and record the PenniLogic visual and interaction direction
items.outcome: One evidence-led visual and interaction world is selected for the product and translated into platform consequences before component or screen teams invent local identity.
items.context: No approved visual authority exists. A finance category default or a patchwork of three platform aesthetics would undermine recognition and trust; premature token selection would harden an untested direction.
scope: Seven grounded candidate worlds spanning multiple material and graphic traditions, excluding category-default fintech dashboards
Concept probes for debt progress, transaction clarification, household privacy and operator urgency
Audience identification, clarity, accessibility, cultural and platform-fit evaluation
Selected thesis, form, signature interaction, content behavior, risks and rejected alternatives
Durable direction contract that T-DSY-01 and platform design tickets consume
acceptance_criteria: Candidates are materially distinct, grounded in product truth and tested with representative users rather than selected from mood-board preference
The chosen direction makes debt progress, provenance, uncertainty and control legible without gamification or shame
Contrast, data density, reduced motion, localization expansion and Material/web/admin adaptation are feasible
The decision records the selected direction, rejected alternatives, evidence, unresolved risks and implementation consequences
The CDO makes and signs the final D2 decision; no platform lead self-approves a separate identity
contracts_schema: Direction record exposes semantic roles and platform consequences but no raw color or component token contract until T-DSY-01
security_privacy: Concept material uses synthetic figures and never depicts unsafe sharing or admin access as ordinary browsing
Trust claims remain evidence-backed and avoid lock, shield or compliance theater
observability: Concept comprehension, identification, task clarity, accessibility defects and unresolved risk disposition
tests: Concept comprehension and preference study with order balancing
rollout_rollback: Direction is selected before token/component finalization
Reversal requires a superseding CDO record and design-system migration plan
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. A small concept team owns probes and decision record; platform squads may assess feasibility but cannot begin independent visual systems.
definition_of_done: Concept evidence and CDO decision merged
Accessibility, Content and platform feasibility reviews recorded
T-DSY-01 and platform tickets reference the selected version
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Define UX outcome metrics, continuous research and design debt governance
items.outcome: Design success is measured through task, comprehension, correction, trust and sustained-progress outcomes with a continuous research cadence rather than aesthetic completion.
items.context: The current plan measures engineering and funnel events, but a design can increase clicks while reducing comprehension or safety. Outcome metrics and research triggers must be selected before instrumentation hardens.
scope: Per-journey task success, time, error, correction, abandonment, comprehension and recovery measures
Guardrails for permission coercion, harmful sharing, support demand, accessibility and dark patterns
Baseline, target, sample limitation and decision threshold format
Continuous research calendar, panel health and trigger-based follow-up
Unmoderated benchmark tasks after moderated defects close and a post-beta longitudinal diary or follow-up protocol
Design debt register with severity, owner, due date and release impact
acceptance_criteria: Every critical journey names one primary outcome and at least one trust or harm guardrail
No success metric rewards permission grant, AI use, subscription or sharing without user benefit and safety context
Telemetry events contain no money, raw content, prompt, identity or household relationship detail
A metric crossing a kill threshold creates a reviewed product decision rather than an automatic nudge
Each critical journey has a versioned unmoderated benchmark and the post-beta longitudinal plan names cohort, cadence, retention, stop criteria and decisions it may change
Open high-severity design debt blocks D8 unless the CDO records a dated exception
contracts_schema: Metric, guardrail, research trigger, design-debt and decision-threshold records linked to journey IDs
security_privacy: Aggregation, minimum cohort, retention and access rules follow T-PLT-03 and privacy consent
No session recording captures financial or operator-sensitive content
observability: This ticket defines the UX observability catalogue and its privacy budget
tests: Unmoderated benchmark reproducibility and longitudinal retention/privacy review
rollout_rollback: Metrics ship disabled until consent, payload and cohort checks pass
Rollback stops collection and retains only approved aggregate history
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. UX Research owns outcome definitions; product analytics implements approved event shapes later and cannot add content fields locally.
definition_of_done: Metric and research governance catalogue merged
Privacy, Product, UX Research and CDO approvals recorded
Coverage and sensitive-payload tests pass
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges
